data.title: Brazil leads LatAm assets higher after cooler-than-expected inflation data
data.description:
Key points:
  • MSCI LatAm stock index rises 3%, FX up 1.3%
  • Argentina's Senate to weigh crucial bill
  • Mexico central bank lifts 2026 growth forecast after stronger third quarter
  • US, Qatar to help Venezuela clear regional development bank arrears, sources say

By Niket Nishant and Johann M Cherian

Brazilian stocks surged on Thursday and were on track for their strongest day in over seven weeks after data showed inflation eased in mid-November, helping investors shrug off the latest tariff threats from Washington.

The Bovespa index was last up 4.4%, the biggest gainer in Latin America, while the real strengthened 1.4% versus the US dollar and 2.1% versus the Mexican peso .

The IPCA-15 consumer price index rose less than expected in the month through mid-November, data showed, raising investor expectations the local central bank could start considering lowering interest rates if the trend continues.

The gains could help investors look past the fresh tariff threat from the US. Washington proposed adding new tariffs on goods from Brazil on Wednesday, ​including a 10% duty on finished aircraft, arguing Brasilia had failed to rectify what it calls "unreasonable" trade practices.

Separately, Brazil's finance minister Dario Durigan said he will hold a follow-up meeting with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva later on Thursday to discuss additional fiscal measures aimed at curbing spending.

MSCI's index of regional equities (.MILA00000PUS) gained 2.9%, while the corresponding currency gauge (.MILA00000CUS) rose 1.3%.

"EM equities look positioned for robust performance in 2027, supported by double-digit earnings growth, inexpensive valuations, an oversold starting point, and structural AI capex tailwinds," JPMorgan analysts wrote in a note.

The brokerage has an "overweight" rating on regional sovereign bonds, but is underweight currencies as it expects the US Federal Reserve to raise rates.

Higher rates in the US typically boost the dollar, thereby weakening emerging market currencies.

ARGENTINA'S SENATE POISED TO SUSPEND PRIMARIES

Argentine stocks (.MMXMRVLGA) shot up 3.2% and the peso gained 0.2% as the country's Senate weighed a bill that would suspend primary elections.

If suspended it would be a potential win for President Javier Milei ahead of next year's presidential race as the country teeters on the brink of a recession.

Mexican stocks shed 1.6% after logging the strongest daily jump since June in the previous session, while the peso slipped 0.6%.

The country's central bank raised its 2026 economic growth forecast to 1.9% after stronger-than-expected activity in the third quarter, even as it warned investment is likely to remain subdued because of uncertainty over trade ties with the United States.

Separately, the country sought a meeting with US aviation authorities to discuss permits for SpaceX to use Mexican airspace and potentially relocate its launch activities, following tensions between Mexico City and Elon Musk's trillion-dollar company.

Peru's sol and stocks (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) were steady after President Keiko Fujimori said the country will receive a $10 billion loan from the Inter-American Development Bank over four years.

Venezuelan bonds were also steady, following a two-day rally on debt restructuring hopes.

The country is also working on separate bridge loans with the US Treasury and Qatar to clear arrears owed to two regional development banks, a move that could unlock fresh multilateral financing for the cash-strapped country, sources told Reuters.

Elsewhere, Turkey's Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said the country expects to complete work to meet MSCI's requirements by the end of December, ahead of the index provider's June 2027 deadline, as Ankara seeks to bring its capital markets in line with international standards after an investment funds crisis.

The country's equities index closed up 0.8% earlier in the day.

Trading was relatively subdued because of the US Thanksgiving holiday.

data.title: Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block
data.description:
Bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov. 26. According to Galaxy's Alex Thorn, it took Bitcoin miners 98 minutes and 19 seconds to find the next block.

That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block. The wait ended at 18:28 UTC on Thursday.

For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.

Even if you paid a very high transaction fee, you would still have to wait until a miner found the next block before your transaction could receive its first confirmation.

Thursday's gap was the 69th longest since 2011, according to Galaxy Research. It was just three minutes shy of the threshold for the top 50.

And this year's other long gap lasted nearly two hours. On July 6, miners took 112 minutes and 26 seconds to find the next block (number 956,953). That was the 19th longest gap on record, according to Galaxy.

How can a 10-minute interval result in a 98-minute wait?

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to keep the average block interval at around 10 minutes.

However, blocks sometimes are found seconds apart. Other times, it takes well over an hour for the next block to be found.

At any given mining difficulty, the chance that a single attempt to find a block will succeed is incredibly small.

If miners have spent 90 minutes trying to find the next block, the chance of succeeding on the next attempt is the same as it was on the first attempt.

So the expected time until the next block is found is still 10 minutes, even if it's already been 90 minutes since the last block was found. That's assuming the network's total computing power and mining difficulty remain unchanged.

Assuming an average block interval of 10 minutes, Thorn said you could expect a gap of at least 98 minutes and 19 seconds about once every 18,600 block intervals.

That means such a gap should occur roughly once every four months, based on an average of about 144 blocks per day.

How the historical rankings can change

Galaxy examined 877,290 block intervals going back to Jan. 1, 2011.

Researchers identified 1,948 intervals where at least an hour had passed between the timestamps of successive blocks.

However, Galaxy flagged 97 of those intervals because an adjacent block had a timestamp that was off by at least 10 minutes. This raised questions about the actual length of those gaps.

The longest recorded interval is particularly interesting.

On Nov. 30, 2011, block 155,290 seemingly marked the end of a 144-minute-and-50-second gap.

However, the miner who found the next block had set its timestamp back by 65 minutes.

After excluding apparent timestamp errors, the longest gap was 141 minutes and one second, recorded on Oct. 13, 2011.

data.title: Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Plunges $6 Billion: The Cost of His Bitcoin Bet
data.description:
Key takeaways

  • Michael Saylor’s estimated net worth has fallen about $6 billion, from $9.3 billion in October 2025 to roughly $3.3 billion on November 25, 2026, a 64.5% drop per Forbes.
  • The $6 billion is a drop in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any asset sales.
  • Saylor’s personal 17,732 BTC (bought for about $175 million) would be worth roughly $1.07 billion at $60,325, assuming he still holds them all.
  • Strategy holds 851,305 BTC bought at an average $75,446, leaving a paper shortfall of about $12.88 billion against its $64.23 billion cost.
  • Strategy’s mNAV was 0.94 at the November 25 close, so raising capital by issuing shares has become harder, and that matters as much as the Bitcoin price.

Michael Saylor’s net worth has fallen by approximately $6 billion since the cryptocurrency market peaked in October 2025. The Strategy co-founder, whose fortune was estimated at $9.3 billion at the time, is now worth around $3.3 billion, according to Forbes.

The decline has wiped out nearly two-thirds of Saylor’s estimated wealth. Yet the billionaire’s company continues to accumulate Bitcoin despite mounting paper losses, showing little willingness to reconsider its investment strategy.

For Saylor, the downturn presents a problem that extends well beyond the price of Bitcoin. Much of his fortune depends on a company that must convince investors to keep financing its accumulation strategy.

How Much Has Michael Saylor Lost During the Bitcoin Crash?

Saylor was already among the cryptocurrency industry’s biggest financial casualties in February, when Forbes estimated that his wealth had fallen by $4.7 billion from its October 2025 level.

His fortune briefly stabilized in the following months, reaching an estimated $4.7 billion in June, before suffering another setback.

Bitcoin’s return to the $60,000 level has added pressure, but the cryptocurrency alone does not explain the scale of the decline. Saylor’s exposure through Strategy makes his financial position considerably more complicated than that of an ordinary Bitcoin investor.

The $6 billion represents a reduction in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any disclosed asset sales.

How Much Bitcoin Does Michael Saylor Personally Own?

In October 2020, Saylor disclosed that he personally owned 17,732 BTC, acquired for approximately $175 million.

At the Bitcoin price of $60,325 reported by Strategy on November 26, those holdings would be worth approximately $1.07 billion, assuming he still owns the entire disclosed amount.

That would leave his original personal investment with an unrealized gain of roughly $895 million.

His current personal Bitcoin balance has not been independently confirmed, but the calculation illustrates an important distinction. Saylor can lose billions in estimated wealth while remaining substantially profitable on his original Bitcoin purchases.

The situation at Strategy is quite different.

Strategy Is Sitting on Nearly $13 Billion in Bitcoin Paper Losses

While Saylor began buying Bitcoin at considerably lower prices, his company has spent much of the past several years increasing its exposure at higher valuations.

According to its November 23 SEC filing, Strategy acquired another 457 BTC for $29.6 million, bringing its total holdings to 851,305 BTC.

The company has spent approximately $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

Its official Bitcoin dashboard valued those reserves at approximately $51.35 billion on November 26.

That leaves a gap of nearly $12.9 billion between the company’s cumulative acquisition cost and the market value of its Bitcoin holdings.

These figures do not represent realized trading losses, nor do they capture the full financial performance of the company.

Nevertheless, the numbers reveal how dramatically the economics of accumulating Bitcoin have changed during the downturn.

Why Saylor’s Fortune Is Vulnerable to More Than Bitcoin

For years, investors were willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares. The attraction was not simply the Bitcoin it owned, but the prospect that management could raise additional capital and increase shareholders’ exposure to the cryptocurrency.

That premium is no longer something the company can take for granted.

Strategy’s dashboard showed an mNAV ratio of 0.94 at the November 25 stock market close, using its own net Bitcoin value per share methodology.

The company’s latest investor briefing acknowledges the implications:

“

A widening discount can cause MSTR to underperform BTC even when bitcoin rises.

Strategy · Investor briefing

This is where Saylor’s investment model faces a more difficult test.

When investors are willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares, raising capital to acquire more Bitcoin can improve the economics of the business. When that premium disappears, issuing additional shares becomes a more complicated proposition.

Strategy’s own sensitivity analysis shows that a Bitcoin price of $40,000 would reduce its estimated net reserve value per share to $45.37, compared with $163.17 at a Bitcoin price of $100,000. The figures illustrate how sensitive the company’s underlying reserve valuation is to Bitcoin price movements.

Strategy’s third-quarter financial results offer a clearer picture of why its cash reserves and financing obligations now matter almost as much as the price of Bitcoin.

Buying more Bitcoin is only one part of the equation. The cost of financing those purchases matters just as much.

Could Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Recover?

There is a credible case for recovery. Strategy still owns more than 850,000 Bitcoin, giving it considerable exposure to any sustained cryptocurrency market rebound.

The company also reported approximately $4.82 billion in combined cash and dollar reserves in its latest investor briefing, providing a buffer against its financing obligations.

But a recovery in Bitcoin would not necessarily produce an equivalent recovery in Saylor’s wealth. Strategy’s share price also depends on its debt, preferred-stock obligations, access to capital and the valuation investors are willing to assign to its business model.

The next test for Saylor is not whether he can buy another thousand Bitcoin. It is whether he can continue financing those purchases on terms that benefit existing shareholders.

His personal fortune has already demonstrated how expensive that distinction can become.

data.title: Fab-Form Industries Ltd. Announces U.S. Patent Office Allowance of Space-R Patent Claims
data.description:
Delta, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Fab-Form Industries Ltd. ("Fab-Form®", or the "Company") is pleased to announce that the United States Patent and Trademark Office ("USPTO") has allowed the patent claims for its innovative SPACE-R product. This allowance represents a significant milestone in the Company's ongoing commitment to innovation, product development and delivering advanced solutions to contractors worldwide. The patent is expected to be formally issued in due course.

SPACE-R addresses three challenges in creating reinforced concrete columns. First, it replaces the traditional horizontal steel stirrup with a lightweight fiberglass component, significantly reducing shipping costs and eliminating corrosion issues. Second, it utilizes polypropylene clips to connect vertical rebar to the horizontal stirrup, reducing onsite labor and eliminating human error. Thirdly, it features polypropylene fins on the outside to ensure the reinforcement is correctly positioned within the column form, a task typically accomplished with rebar wheels in the industry.

ABSTRACT OF THE DISCLOSUREThere is provided a formwork assembly. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of longitudinally-extending and laterally spaced-apart steel reinforcing bars. The formwork assembly includes a hoop reinforcement shaped to extend about the reinforcing bars. The hoop reinforcement is configured to provide shear strength to concrete poured into the formwork so positioned. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of receptacles circumferentially spaced-apart about, coupled to and radially inwardly-extending from the hoop reinforcement so as to promote a desired positioning or spacing of the reinforcing bars. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of spacers circumferentially spaced-apart about, coupled to and radially outwardly-extending from the hoop reinforcement. The formwork assembly includes a formwork shaped to extend about and be positioned in place via the plurality of spacers. There is further provided a concrete stirrup apparatus comprising said hoop reinforcement, receptacles and spacers.

data.title: Japan weighs tighter oversight of DeFi, self-custodial wallets
data.description:
Japan’s Financial Services Agency (FSA) is weighing potential new regulations for decentralized finance (DeFi) and self-custodial wallet providers as part of a broader effort to address risks associated with onchain finance.

In a discussion paper dated Thursday, the regulator raised the possibility of discouraging users from accessing DeFi services that lack adequate Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing controls.

The FSA also asked whether regulated businesses that interact with DeFi, including stablecoin issuers, on- and off-ramp providers and financial institutions, should play a role in mitigating illicit finance risks when no party responsible for regulatory compliance can be identified.

The regulator questioned how to identify parties responsible for DeFi services that claim to be decentralized but retain centralized elements, and whether front-end providers that give users access to decentralized exchanges should be subject to financial regulation.

The question of who should be held responsible for DeFi activities remains unresolved in other major markets. The European Union excludes fully decentralized crypto services without intermediaries from its Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation, while US regulators have largely focused on the nature of financial activities and the degree of control exercised by developers or operators. The stalled US CLARITY Act seeks to clarify which DeFi participants should be subject to financial regulation.

Japan weighs safeguards for self-custodial wallets

The FSA noted that direct regulation of self-custodial wallet use and providers that solely develop or sell software or hardware remains uncommon internationally but raised questions about whether additional measures are needed to protect users and prevent illicit financial activity.

Japan already requires domestic virtual asset service providers to collect information and maintain records on transactions involving self-custodial wallets, according to the FSA. Potential anti-fraud measures also include cooling-off periods for transfers from newly opened crypto exchange accounts to self-custodial wallets.

The discussions form part of a broader financial strategy announced by the FSA in July to promote onchain finance, with the initiative’s interim findings targeted for early 2027.

data.title: NOTICE TO ATTEND THE EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING OF G5 ENTERTAINMENT AB (PUBL)
data.description:
The shareholders of G5 Entertainment AB (publ), reg. no 556680-8878 (the "Company") are hereby summoned to attend the Extraordinary General Meeting to be held at 9:00 am (CET) on Tuesday, December 22, 2026, at Eversheds Sutherland Advokatbyrå's office on Sveavägen 20, 3rd floor, 111 57 Stockholm. Registration begins at 8:45 am (CET).

The board of directors has decided that shareholders shall be able to exercise their voting rights by postal vote prior to the meeting pursuant to Chapter 7, Section 4 a of the Swedish Companies Act (2005:551) and Article 10 of the Company's Articles of Association. Shareholders may thus choose to participate in the meeting either by physical attendance, in person or by proxy, or by postal vote.

General requirements for participation

Shareholders who wish to attend the Extraordinary General Meeting must:

  • be recorded as shareholders in the share register maintained by Euroclear Sweden AB on Monday, December 14, 2026; and
  • in order to have the right to attend the Extraordinary General Meeting, request to be temporarily registered in the share register kept by Euroclear Sweden AB, if the shareholder's shares are nominee-registered. The shareholder must instruct their nominee thereof in due time prior to Wednesday, December 16, 2026, on which date such registration must be executed.

Requirements for participation by physical presence

Shareholders who wish to attend the Extraordinary General Meeting in person or by proxy must, no later than Wednesday, December 16, 2026, have given the Company notice of their participation. Notice to the Extraordinary General Meeting can be made via a digital form available at: https://stamma.corplean.com/g5-entertainment-2026-12-22?lang=en. The notice must, when applicable, include information regarding any representative, proxy and/or a maximum of two advisors.

Proxy

Shareholders represented by proxy shall issue a written and dated power of attorney to the proxy signed by the shareholder. A power of attorney issued by a legal entity shall have a copy of registration certificate attached, or if such certificate does not exist, equivalent authorization document. A power of attorney form for shareholders who wish to participate in the general meeting by proxy is available on the Company's website (https://corporate.g5.com/). The power of attorney and the registration certificate may not be issued earlier than one year before the date of the general meeting, with the exception of where the power of attorney specifies a longer period, up to a maximum of five years. The original power of attorney and any registration certificate must be available at the Extraordinary General Meeting and copies of the documents should, in due time before the general meeting, be sent to Eversheds Sutherland at the address above.

Requirements for participation by postal vote in advance

Shareholders intending to vote by postal vote only must submit their votes no later than Wednesday, December 16, 2026, through a digital postal voting form available at: https://stamma.corplean.com/g5-entertainment-2026-12-22?lang=en. Natural shareholders or, if applicable, authorized representatives of shareholders who are legal persons, identify themselves by using BankID or other secure signing solution in conjunction with the submitting of the postal voting form (detailed instructions, terms and instructions for postal voting are stated in the form). A postal vote may be cancelled up to and including December 16, 2026 by sending an e-mail to support@corplean.com. If two or more forms have the same dating, only the last received form will be taken into account.

The shareholder cannot provide other instructions than by marking an answer for each item in the form. If the shareholder has provided the form with special instructions or conditions, or changed or added to the pre-printed text, the postal vote is invalid. Further instructions can be found in the postal voting form.

Proposed agenda

  • Opening of the meeting
  • Election of chairman of the meeting
  • Preparation and approval of voting register
  • Presentation and approval of the agenda
  • Election of one or two persons to verify the minutes together with the chairman
  • Determination of whether the meeting has been duly convened
  • Resolution on a voluntary redemption program comprising (a) reduction of the share capital by way of redemption of shares for repayment to the shareholders and (b) increase of the share capital by way of bonus issue
  • Resolutions on (a) reduction of the share capital by way of cancellation of own shares and (b) increase of the share capital by way of bonus issue
  • Resolution to authorize the board of directors to undertake minor adjustments of the resolutions
  • Closure of the meeting

The board's proposals for resolutions

Item 2 – Election of chairman of the meeting

The board of directors proposes that the Chairman of the Board, Petter Nylander, is appointed as chairman of the meeting.

Item 3 – Preparation and approval of the voting register

The proposed voting register is the voting register that will have been prepared based on the shareholders present, the share register of the general meeting, and the postal votes received and that has been checked and approved by the persons elected to verify the minutes.

Item 7 – Resolution on a voluntary redemption program

Background and rationale

The purpose of the proposed redemption program is to reduce the number of shares in the Company and to return capital that is not deemed necessary for the business to the shareholders. The Company's repurchases of own shares are currently limited by the low liquidity of the share, which has meant that the Company has not been able to utilize its authorization to acquire own shares to the desired extent. A voluntary redemption program makes it possible to acquire and cancel a larger number of shares in a single structured transaction, on equal terms for all shareholders. The program gives each shareholder the opportunity to choose whether to have shares redeemed or to retain their shareholding.

Through the cost savings implemented during 2026, the group is profitable and the Company has a strong financial position without interest-bearing liabilities other than lease liabilities. The group has reduced the number of its own new games under development, and user acquisition to scale up a successful new game is deemed to be possible to finance with remaining funds and cash flow from operations. Furthermore, the distribution of third-party games on the G5 Store is a less capital-intensive business. The board of directors considers that the Company, also after the redemption program, will have a good equity ratio and satisfactory liquidity. For the board's assessment of the justifiability of the repayment, reference is made to the board's statement pursuant to Chapter 20, Section 8 of the Swedish Companies Act.

The board of directors proposes that the general meeting resolves on a voluntary redemption program of a total of not more than SEK 84,311,360 in accordance with items 7 (a) and 7 (b) below. The resolutions are conditional upon each other and are proposed to be adopted as one joint resolution.

An information brochure describing the voluntary redemption program in more detail will be published before trading in redemption rights and the application period commence.

Item 7 (a) – Reduction of the share capital by way of redemption of shares for repayment to the shareholders

The board of directors proposes that the general meeting resolves that the Company's share capital shall be reduced by not more than SEK 122,269.21 for repayment to the shareholders. The reduction shall be effected through redemption of not more than 1,053,892 ordinary shares, each with a quota value of approximately SEK 0.116. The repayment to the shareholders shall amount to a total of not more than SEK 84,311,360.

The reduction shall be carried out through a voluntary redemption program. Each ordinary share in the Company entitles the holder to one (1) redemption right. All holders of redemption rights are entitled to an equal right to redeem ordinary shares. No redemption rights, and thus no right to redeem shares, are received for class C shares or for ordinary shares held by the Company.

data.title: Stacks Labs is researching a way to borrow against Bitcoin without handing it over
data.description:
Stacks Labs is researching a design that would let Bitcoin holders borrow stablecoins against their BTC without giving up custody of it.

The coins would stay timelocked under the holder's control and keep earning yield.

The concept builds on Stacks' protocol bonds, which are anchored on the Bitcoin base layer. Users who stake BTC through these bonds would be able to borrow stablecoins against that staked position.

The BTC would remain locked, not transferred to a lender or a custodian. Under the proposed design, BTC used as collateral would continue to earn returns while it sits locked.

Stacks has said the lending mechanism draws on the infrastructure behind Zest Protocol. Zest has carried out over 1,500 liquidations without incurring bad debt.

That record is relevant because liquidations are where lending protocols tend to break. When collateral prices fall fast, a lender needs to close out risky positions before a loan is worth more than what backs it. Doing that more than 1,500 times with zero bad debt suggests the system has been tested under real conditions.

Bitcoin staking through protocol bonds launched on September 10, 2026. Self-custodial borrowing against staked BTC is planned for 2027.

As of mid-November 2026, three protocol bonds had drawn approximately 1,735-1,740 BTC, with major institutions among the participants.

Those bonds offer a targeted yield of 3% per year.

Stacks also has infrastructure goals tied to the lending rollout. The network aims for throughput improvements of up to 100 times current capacity. It also wants deeper stablecoin liquidity through its planned USDCx initiative.

The institutional interest in protocol bonds hints at who this is built for. If roughly 1,735-1,740 BTC has already been committed to a 3% target yield, a borrowing layer on top could make those positions more useful. Holders would earn yield and still be able to draw liquidity against the same coins.

There are real caveats. This is a research design with a 2027 target, not a live product.

The supporting infrastructure also has to arrive. The 100x throughput goal and USDCx liquidity are plans, and the lending market's usefulness depends heavily on both.

Liquidation mechanics also deserve close attention. Zest's record of over 1,500 liquidations with no bad debt is encouraging. But a self-custodial, timelocked structure raises its own design questions, particularly around how a protocol enforces repayment on collateral that stays in the user's hands.

The 2027 borrowing rollout will be the real test. Watch for progress on throughput upgrades, the arrival of USDCx liquidity and any published details on how liquidations would work for collateral that never leaves its owner's custody.

data.title: Peru's Fujimori announces $16 billion loan package
data.description:
Peru's President Keiko Fujimori said on Thursday that the country will receive a total of $16 billion in loans from the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) and the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF).

The IDB has approved a $10 billion loan for the country, while the CAF has greenlit a $6 billion package, according to Fujimori, who spoke to journalists at a business forum in Cusco.

Fujimori said the IDB's loan will be dispersed over four years, with $4 billion going to the private sector.

data.title: Euronext Athens Holding S.A. to merge with, and into, Euronext N.V.
data.description:
Euronext Athens Holding S.A. to merge with, and into, Euronext N.V.

  • Euronext N.V. and Euronext Athens Holding S.A. have decided to pursue a cross-border Merger by which Euronext N.V. will absorb Euronext Athens Holding S.A.
  • The Merger simplifies the legal structure of the Group and facilitates the integration of the Greek market within the Euronext Group
  • The Merger offers improved financial terms for Euronext Athens Holding S.A. shareholders:
    • One (1) new Euronext share per seventeen (17) Euronext Athens shares, compared to the one (1) Euronext share per twenty (20) Euronext Athens shares under Euronext’s 2025 Voluntary Tender Offer
    • Based on Euronext’s closing price of €167.50 as of 25 November 2026, the proposed Exchange Ratio values Euronext Athens at €9.85 per share1, (+38%) compared to €7.14 under Euronext’s 2025 Voluntary Tender Offer2
    • A cash-exit right of €9.29 per share provided for each shareholder exercising the withdrawal right
  • Extraordinary general meetings of both companies are scheduled for 26 January 2027

Amsterdam, Athens, Brussels, Dublin, Lisbon, Milan, Oslo and Paris – 26 November 2026 – Euronext N.V. (“Euronext”), the leading European capital market infrastructure and Euronext Athens Holding S.A. (“Euronext Athens”) jointly announce that the Managing Board of Euronext, with the approval of its Supervisory Board, and the Board of Directors of Euronext Athens have approved and drawn up a joint cross-border merger proposal (the “Merger Proposal”) to pursue a cross-border statutory merger by which Euronext, as acquiring company, will absorb Euronext Athens, as disappearing company (the “Merger”) .

Rationale for the Merger

The Merger is the next step after the successful completion of the exchange offer in November 2025. The rationale of the Merger is to allow the full integration of Euronext Athens into the Euronext group (the “Group”) to achieve operational, commercial, organisational and financial benefits for the Group, the shareholders and other stakeholders of Euronext Athens and for the clients of the Greek market.

Moreover:

(i) the Merger simplifies the legal structure of the Group and the costs of a separate listing are eliminated;

(ii) the Merger facilitates the integration of the Greek market within the Group;

(iii) the Group is better equipped to finance the required investment in the Greek market infrastructure; and

(iv) the Merger provides a simpler corporate and disclosure framework with a single listed issuer at the level of the Group.

The Merger does not change the supervisory allocation applicable to the Greek market: Greek regulated markets and post-trade activities will continue to be conducted by Greek-licensed entities under the supervision of the relevant Greek authorities.

Through the Merger, Euronext Athens shareholders who receive Euronext shares will become shareholders of Euronext and will participate in the future performance of a larger and more diversified pan-European capital markets infrastructure group. They are expected to benefit from greater liquidity in Euronext shares and broader exposure across the Group’s activities and geographies, while retaining an economic interest in the continued development of the Greek capital market within Euronext.

Structure and terms of the Merger

The Merger will be effected in accordance with the applicable EU framework for cross-border mergers, as implemented in the Netherlands in articles 2:309 et seq. and 2:333b et seq. DCC of the Dutch Civil Code and in Greece in articles 53a et seq. of the Greek Company Transformation Act (Greek Law 4601/2019, as amended “GCTA”). On the date the Merger becomes effective (the “Effective Date”), Euronext Athens will cease to exist, without going into liquidation, Euronext will acquire all its assets and liabilities under universal title of succession, and the shares of Euronext Athens will be cancelled and delisted from the regulated market operated by Euronext Athens Single Member S.A. (formerly Athens Stock Exchange). As from the Effective Date, Euronext will continue the activities of Euronext Athens through a branch in Greece.

Under the proposed Merger, one (1) new ordinary share in Euronext, each with a nominal value of EUR 1.60, will be allotted for every seventeen (17) Euronext Athens shares not held by or on behalf of Euronext or Euronext Athens (the “Exchange Ratio”).

The Exchange Ratio represents an enhanced consideration for Euronext Athens shareholders compared to the previous voluntary share exchange tender offer completed in November 2025 which was made on the basis of one (1) ordinary share in Euronext for every twenty (20) Euronext Athens shares.

No fractional shares will be issued. Any entitlement to a fraction of a Euronext share resulting from the application of the Exchange Ratio will be settled in cash in accordance with the mechanism set out in the Merger Proposal.

The allotted shares will participate in full in the profits of Euronext as of the Effective Date.

Any shareholder of Euronext Athens who votes against the Merger and who does not wish to receive ordinary shares in the capital of Euronext may exercise a withdrawal right, in accordance with Greek law, giving an entitlement to receive a cash compensation. The proposed cash compensation amounts to EUR 9.29 per ordinary share in the capital of Euronext Athens.

KPMG Accountants N.V., as Dutch auditor, has issued a certificate on, among other things, the reasonableness of the Exchange Ratio, and Ernst & Young (Hellas) Certified Auditors Accountants S.A., as independent expert under Article 53f GCTA, has issued a report on the adequacy of the Exchange Ratio.

The articles of association of Euronext will not be amended in connection with the Merger. The Merger is governed by Dutch law to the fullest extent permitted by law, with matters subject to mandatory provisions of Greek law applicable to Euronext Athens governed by Greek law.

Conditions

Completion of the Merger is subject to (i) approval of the Merger Proposal by the general meetings of Euronext and Euronext Athens, (ii) completion of the publication, filing, creditor-protection and other procedures required under Dutch and Greek law, and (iii) issuance of the Greek pre-merger certificate.

Next steps and timetable

The extraordinary general meetings of Euronext and Euronext Athens resolving on the Merger are scheduled to be held on 26 January 2027.

The Merger Proposal will be filed on 27 November 2026, and its filing is expected to be published in the Dutch State Gazette and on the Greek Commercial Register (GEMI) electronic platform on 1 December 2026. The three-month creditor opposition periods under Dutch law and under Article 53θ GCTA are expected to end on 2 March 2027.

Following issuance of the Greek pre-merger certificate, the Dutch notarial deed of merger will be executed, and the Merger will become effective on the day following its execution.

This timetable is indicative and may change. Euronext will inform the market of the date of execution of the notarial deed of merger, the Effective Date and the expected delivery date of the allotted shares in accordance with applicable law.

Availability of documents

As from 26 November 2026, the Merger Proposal, the board reports of Euronext and Euronext Athens, the certificate of KPMG Accountants N.V. and the report of Ernst & Young (Hellas) Certified Auditors Accountants S.A. as independent experts, the annual accounts of both companies for the financial years 2023, 2024 and 2025, the notification to shareholders and creditors and the withdrawal request form for Euronext Athens shareholders will be made available at the registered offices and on the corporate websites of Euronext (www.euronext.com) and Euronext Athens (www.athens.euronext.com).

Euronext has also published an exemption document in connection with the Merger, pursuant to Articles 1(4)(g) and 1(5)(f) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, which is available on its website. The exemption document does not constitute a prospectus within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 and has not been approved by the Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets (Autoriteit Financiële Markten AFM), the Greek Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC) or any other supervisory authority.

data.title: Turkey's capital markets catch cold from funds crisis
data.description:
Key points:
  • More than 130 funds were liquidated in September
  • Fund collapse led to wave of arrests and lawsuits
  • Regulators had lost expertise and qualified staff, sources say
  • IPOs have dried up, corporate bond issuance has dipped
  • Restoring confidence in regulators is crucial, sources say

By Ebru Tuncay, Mirac Dereli and Aidan Lewis

Turkey needs to overhaul its financial regulators after an investment fund scandal that has sent a chill through the country's capital markets, five bankers and a former senior official said.

The crisis centres on groups of funds that poured money into thinly traded stocks, swelling the value of their assets to more than $20 billion and generating extraordinary returns before they became unable to meet withdrawal demands and were liquidated.

Since September, regulatory officials and other prominent financial figures have been caught up in resignations, dismissals and arrests amid allegations of market manipulation, fraud and bribery that have shaken faith in Turkish capital markets.

Turkey's Capital Markets Board (SPK) approved 33 initial public offerings in the first nine months of 2026, almost double the 18 approved in the whole of the previous year.

Since the funds' collapse, as market conditions and confidence deteriorated, none have been approved, despite 119 companies registered as awaiting SPK approval for flotation.

Restoring trust needs to start with the right appointments, Ramazan Basak, a former deputy chairman of Turkey's Financial Crimes Investigation Board, told Reuters.

"These institutions should be led by people who know the sector well, have a reputation for integrity and have no political ties," he said in an interview.

Those detained in recent weeks include several senior former officials from the SPK and Turkey's Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (BDDK).

Prosecutors are also set to investigate Sahap Kavcioglu, a former central bank governor who announced his resignation as head of the BDDK this month and has denied wrongdoing.

One senior banker said the problems stemmed from appointments at bodies including the BDDK and the SPK, although he added that the institutions themselves were sound.

The BDDK declined to comment. The SPK and the Finance Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

The BDDK had played a major role in putting the banking sector on a sound footing after a 2001 crisis, but had later taken a more passive stance, a second senior banker said.

One problem faced by regulatory authorities over recent years was an exodus of staff to the private sector because of worsening relative pay and conditions, a person in the banking sector said. That led to a shortage of expertise, an executive at a portfolio management company said.

On Thursday, Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said at a press conference that the SPK's powers to intervene against problematic funds were being strengthened and that Turkey was working to meet MSCI Emerging Markets Index requirements by the end of the year.

RIPPLE EFFECT

Some observers have said the crisis was allowed to brew despite public warnings of market manipulation. But once it broke, swift action by authorities contained any systemic risk, against a backdrop of economic challenges including higher energy prices due to the Iran war, analysts said. Last week, Turkey's foreign reserves dropped to their lowest level since 2024 on a net basis.

"In the past at times of stress in the Turkish economy, Turkish households would start exchanging their savings into hard currency, maybe buy more gold as an insurance," said Magdalena Polan, head of emerging markets macroeconomic research at PGIM.

"Outside of a small wobble in some flows in the FX market from the households, we actually did not see that at all."

While consumer confidence dipped to 84.8 in October from 91.9 in September, it has edged back up to 86.8 this month, data from Turkey's state statistics agency shows.

But the crisis has jolted capital markets. Istanbul's main stock exchange index has fallen more than 18% since September 16, the day before the SPK ordered the liquidation of 131 funds. That exceeds a 1.5% dip in European stocks , and the AI-driven 15% drop in MSCI's global emerging market index CBOE:EFS.

A secondary public offering by Turkey's third-largest state-owned lender, Halkbank, and an IPO for state-owned Islamic bank Emlak Katilim Bankasi have been postponed and no public offerings are likely before spring 2027, a fourth person in the banking sector said.

Halkbank did not respond to a request for comment. Emlak Katilim Bankasi declined to comment.

Meanwhile, the number of corporate bonds issued in October dropped to 74, from 102 in September and 119 in August, the Turkish Capital Markets Association said.

The political impact has also been spreading, with those detained or resigning including figures with strong links to Turkey's ruling AK Party (AKP).

The AKP did not respond to a request for comment.

Nearly 130 people had been formally arrested as of last week, said Justice Minister Akin Gurlek, adding that the structure behind the scheme was "not limited to simple stock market manipulation or stock market fraud, but is a comprehensive criminal organization".

President Tayyip Erdogan said last week there would be "not the slightest compromise" on holding those responsible to account and the government had prioritised paying back small investors. Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said on Thursday that 199 billion lira ($3.93 billion) had been paid back, and that authorities would take steps to protect investors.

'MADE TO BEG FOR OUR OWN MONEY'

Savers among the nearly half a million who invested in the funds are angry over what they see as corruption.

At a protest outside the SPK headquarters in Ankara last week attended by several hundred people, some savers demanded full repayment, with several describing how they unsuccessfully sought to sell their investments as the funds imploded.

"We have been made to beg for our own money," said Murat Galip Alparslan, a roofer, adding that he had lost 26 years of his own savings as well as money saved by his mother.

"My family's future has been stolen," he said.

It is unclear what the total loss to investors will be, with claims leading to a wave of legal action.

Criminal complaints are being filed over trades in stocks that took place up to two years ago and should have been referred to prosecutors much sooner, said Basak, who expects "hundreds of trades" to come under scrutiny in court.

data.title: The board of directors of G5 Entertainment AB (publ) proposes a voluntary redemption programme of approximately SEK 84.3 million and convenes an extraordinary general meeting
data.description:
The board of directors of G5 Entertainment AB (publ) ("G5" or the "Company") has today resolved to propose that an extraordinary general meeting on December 22, 2026 resolves on a voluntary redemption programme under which a maximum of 1,053,892 ordinary shares, corresponding to approximately 14.3 percent of the outstanding ordinary shares, may be redeemed at a redemption amount of SEK 80 per share, in total a maximum of approximately SEK 84.3 million. The redemption amount corresponds to a premium of approximately [10] percent compared to the volume-weighted average price of G5’s ordinary share on Nasdaq Stockholm during the ten trading days preceding today’s resolution. The board of directors also proposes that the meeting resolves on the cancellation of 300,000 own ordinary shares held by the Company. The notice of the extraordinary general meeting is published through a separate press release.

Summary

  • Voluntary redemption programme of a maximum total of approximately SEK 84.3 million, where each shareholder chooses whether shares are to be redeemed or retained.
  • A maximum of 1,053,892 ordinary shares, corresponding to approximately 14.3 percent of the outstanding ordinary shares, may be redeemed.
  • The redemption amount is SEK 80 per share, corresponding to a premium of approximately 10 percent on the volume-weighted average price during the ten trading days preceding today’s resolution.
  • Trading in redemption rights and redemption shares will be arranged on Nasdaq Stockholm.
  • The board of directors also proposes the cancellation of 300,000 own ordinary shares held by the Company, combined with a bonus issue so that the share capital remains unchanged.
  • The Company’s ongoing repurchases of its own ordinary shares under the authorisation from the annual general meeting have been paused pending the redemption programme.
  • The extraordinary general meeting will be held on December 22, 2026.

Background and rationale

The purpose of the proposed redemption programme is to reduce the number of shares in the Company and to return capital that is not deemed necessary for the business to the shareholders. The Company’s repurchases of its own shares are currently limited by the low liquidity of the share, which has meant that the Company has not been able to utilise its authorisation to acquire its own shares to the desired extent. A voluntary redemption programme makes it possible to acquire and cancel a larger number of shares in a single structured transaction, on equal terms for all shareholders.

As a result of the cost savings implemented during 2026, the group is profitable and the Company has a strong financial position with no interest-bearing liabilities other than lease liabilities. The board of directors considers that any future investments in user acquisition can be financed with remaining funds and the cash flow from operations, and the distribution of third-party games on the G5 Store is a less capital-intensive business. The board of directors considers that the Company will have a sound equity ratio and satisfactory liquidity also after the redemption programme.

The redemption programme in brief

The redemption programme is carried out through a reduction of the share capital by way of redemption of shares for repayment to the shareholders, combined with a bonus issue restoring the share capital. Each ordinary share in G5 entitles the holder to one (1) redemption right. Seven (7) redemption rights entitle the holder to redeem one (1) ordinary share. Shares held by the Company and class C shares do not carry any redemption rights.

The record date for receipt of redemption rights is proposed to be January 4, 2027. The part of the redemption amount that exceeds the quota value of the shares will be taken from the Company’s unrestricted equity.

Shareholders who do not wish to participate may sell their redemption rights. Shareholders who neither sell nor exercise their redemption rights will retain their shareholding unchanged. Redemption rights that are not exercised or sold during the application period will lapse without value.

An information brochure with complete terms and instructions will be published on the Company’s website before trading in redemption rights and the application period commence.

The timing of trading in redemption shares and payment assumes that the Swedish Companies Registration Office registers the resolutions in time. The redemption is conditional upon the extraordinary general meeting resolving in accordance with the board of directors’ proposal and the resolutions being registered with the Swedish Companies Registration Office.

Cancellation of own shares

The board of directors also proposes that the meeting resolves on a reduction of the share capital through the cancellation of 300,000 own ordinary shares that have been repurchased under authorisations from previous general meetings, combined with a bonus issue so that the share capital remains unchanged.

Extraordinary general meeting

The resolutions require the support of shareholders representing at least two-thirds of both the votes cast and the shares represented at the meeting. The notice of the extraordinary general meeting, including the board of directors’ complete proposals, will be published separately and will be available on the Company’s website, https://corporate.g5.com/.

data.title: Thanksgiving storm knocks out power, disrupts flights on US East Coast
data.description:
A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the US East Coast on Thursday, knocking out power for hundreds of thousands of users as wind gusts of up to 70 mph (112 kph) toppled trees and power lines.

Heavy rains flooded coastal areas, while utilities warned that rain-soaked ground and strong winds could increase the risk of falling trees and power outages.

Nearly 200,000 homes and businesses had no power in Virginia and another 177,000 in Maryland as of 2:26 p.m. ET (1926 GMT), according to poweroutage.us, which also showed Pennsylvania, New Jersey and North Carolina each had tens of thousands of utility customers without electricity.

Utilities and state officials had warned the combination of strong onshore winds and rain could cause widespread power disruptions.

Wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph were reported or forecast across parts of Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and coastal New England, according to the US National Weather Service.

New York City Emergency Management reported winds intensified on Thursday afternoon, reaching 56 mph (90 kph) at LaGuardia Airport.

The NWS said strong onshore winds associated with the storm, combined with king tides, were causing coastal flooding in low-lying communities along portions of the East Coast.

The threat of storms had already led officials to postpone Thursday's 100th edition of the annual Macy's ​Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City, marking the first time the event has been rescheduled due to severe weather.

The storm also disrupted holiday air travel, with more than 400 US flights canceled and some 1,600 delayed by early on Thursday afternoon, according to FlightAware. Major airports in the Washington and New York City areas were among the hardest hit.

"A powerful coastal storm will continue to bring severe impacts to the region through today into this evening due to damaging high winds accompanied by heavy rainfall," the NWS said. "The storm departs overnight into Friday."
